attributes.proposal_description:
Zekret delivers a modular compliance and identity layer for Web3 — enabling the deployment of regulated DeFi, stablecoins, and tokenized assets within MiCA-aligned, privacy-first architectures.

This proposal will bring Zekret’s infrastructure stack to the Cardano ecosystem through selective integration of core modules and delivering custom SDKs, node APIs, and deployment guides for developers and institutional partners.  Zekret provides licensed access and partnership-driven deployment of its core tooling — ensuring compliance, privacy, and security are maintained at the highest level.

Zekret is a modular Layer 3 compliance framework. Offering real-time enforcement of programmable compliance, jurisdiction-aware asset controls, and institutional-grade identity tooling — all without sacrificing decentralization or user privacy. The stack is built to align with MiCA, GDPR, FATF, and local regulatory frameworks while maintaining flexibility for permissionless environments.

This proposal focuses on delivering the following key components:

- zk-ID SDK — A privacy-preserving, off-chain identity module with jurisdiction detection

- Watchtower-as-a-Service — Licensed transaction monitoring and compliance scoring APIs

- Permissioning SDK — Smart contract tools to enforce regulatory rules (e.g., cross-border access logic)

In addition, Zekret will provide:

- Documentation and dev onboarding materials via GitBook and private portal access

- Technical support for early adopters and regulated dApps in the Cardano ecosystem

- Participation in Intersect-led workshops and discussions around MiCA and compliance tooling

- A pilot deployment path for institutional node partners and regulated builders

The goal is to unlock Cardano-native adoption of compliant infrastructure — allowing dApps, wallets, bridges, and asset issuers to build with legal certainty and jurisdictional logic already embedded. Zekret’s approach enables institutional trust without undermining the values of decentralization and user privacy.

The Zekret team includes former UK FCA executives, CBDC sandbox contributors, legal architects, and protocol engineers — with active deployments planned in Europe, LATAM, and APAC. Through this proposal, Zekret seeks to establish Cardano as a preferred ecosystem for regulated Web3 innovation.

Deliverables:

✔ Test suite and validator support logic

Phase 3 – Developer Pilots & Node Deployment

- Work with Intersect Product and Technical Steering Committees on roadmap alignment

- Explore inclusion in national sandbox programs and public-private pilots

Deliverables:

Deliverables:

attributes.problem_statement:
Despite the increasing maturity of the Cardano ecosystem, regulatory uncertainty remains one of the biggest barriers to real-world adoption of decentralized finance, tokenized assets, and identity-based applications.
Builders, institutions, and even governments are seeking to launch solutions on-chain — but cannot proceed without a framework for compliance, identity verification, and transaction-level governance. Current tools either compromise privacy or require centralization, undermining the foundational principles of Cardano.
Without modular, jurisdiction-aware infrastructure that supports programmable enforcement (e.g., MiCA compliance, KYC/AML scoring, travel rules, and auditability), the ecosystem risks becoming inaccessible to regulated entities — and unable to capitalize on the next wave of institutional and civic adoption.
Zekret addresses this gap by providing a Layer 3 compliance and privacy infrastructure — interoperable with Cardano — that enables builders to deploy legally operable and privacy-preserving systems while preserving decentralization. The lack of such tooling is a critical bottleneck for builders, stablecoin issuers, public pilots, and DeFi protocols looking to scale within or beyond Cardano.
attributes.proposal_benefit:
If implemented, this proposal will unlock regulatory operability and institutional adoption pathways for the Cardano ecosystem, without compromising decentralization or user privacy.

Zekret introduces a modular Layer 3 compliance and identity infrastructure that can be integrated into existing Cardano-based applications, wallets, dApps, and chains. By providing builders with access to tools like zk-ID onboarding, risk-based permissioning, and jurisdiction-aware audit scoring, this solution removes one of the most persistent roadblocks to real-world, large-scale adoption: regulatory readiness.
Benefits to Specific Community Segments:

1. Protocol Developers and Builders
- Can integrate compliance tooling (e.g. travel-rule enforcement, MiCA alignment) into existing DeFi, dApp, or wallet stacks
- Gain access to SDKs and APIs that allow permissioned asset flow or onboarding logic
- Shorter go-to-market cycles and fewer legal uncertainties

2. Stablecoin & RWA Projects
- Ability to issue assets aligned with MiCA, FATF, and GDPR standards
- Interoperability with identity systems and regulated custody infrastructure
- Support for institutional onramps and offramps

3. Institutions, Custodians, and Gateways
Infrastructure to operate compliance-focused nodes (Institutional, Watchtower Nodes)
Deployment of fiat ramps, token bridges, and scoring engines within a decentralized framework
Revenue-sharing opportunities via node license or compliance-as-a-service

attributes.comment_text:
Zekret appears to be a highly promising compliance framework, especially for aligning with MiCA/FATF standards as a Layer 3 infrastructure compatible with Cardano. That said, the current proposal seems to be in a relatively early phase of integration with the Cardano ecosystem — more of a pilot or proof-of-concept stage than a production deployment.

With that in mind, could you please clarify:

Why did you choose to request Core funding at this stage of the project, rather than submitting it through a more risk-tolerant program like Project Catalyst?

What specific criteria or strategic rationale led you to conclude that this proposal fits the mandate of the Core budget, which is often reserved for critical infrastructure and roadmap-aligned initiatives?

What are the specific KPIs and success criteria defined for each phase of this proposal? What tangible deliverables would constitute success at the end of the 9-month timeline, from the community’s perspective?

How will progress be measured toward eventual commercial use and adoption within the Cardano ecosystem?

Are there quantifiable indicators of success, such as number of pilot deployments, node operations on testnet, or SDK usage?

Are the zk-ID and Watchtower components compatible with Cardano’s smart contract architecture ? Have you received specific feedback or endorsements from developers within the Cardano ecosystem (e.g., dApp or infrastructure developers)? What is the extent of engagement with the Technical Steering Committee (TSC)? Was this proposal technically reviewed before submission?

How has this proposal been socialized and discussed on platforms such as X (Twitter), Discord?

How does the Zekret team plan to maintain the SDKs and node APIs after the proposal is completed?

What value (e.g., increase in TVL, active dApps using the tooling) is expected to be brought to the Cardano chain in return for ₳1,587,300? Is the budget allocation reasonable when compared with similar-sized infrastructure proposals?

Is it all open source?

While the Zekret proposal aligns with Cardano's strategic direction and is timely given the current regulatory environment, several challenges remain to be addressed:

The appropriateness of the funding method given the project's early stage of development
The need for clear KPIs and measurable return on investment metrics
Demonstration of compatibility with Cardano's technical architecture
Expansion of community support and engagement

Considering that the requested budget is relatively small and the proposal addresses the critical issue of regulatory compliance, it can be conditionally evaluated as appropriate for the 2025 budget. However, clear answers and concrete plans addressing the above challenges should be prerequisites for approval.
I totally agree that Cardano urgently needs private compliance systems for institutions but should it be at cost of funding a potentially closed-source, license-gated infrastructure layer?

While the implementation of a Layer 3 solution aimed at regulatory operability and institutional adoption could significantly accelerate the growth of Cardano if successful, the proposed 9-month timeline appears overly ambitious. Additionally, the lack of clearly defined KPIs, especially during the early adoption phase, raises concerns about the project's ability to deliver a fully operational solution.

From reading your proposal and website, it seems this project is still in the early stages (more information about your token than the technoology and how it relates to Cardano in particular). Wording like "layer 3" is also weird given you don't mention what is the L2 in this case

Overall, given the for-profit nature of this, the lack of clarity on how this would integrate on Cardano and the early stages of the project, I am voting no, but you're welcome to resubmit in the future once your project is more mature

Thank you for the question Sebastien.

While our public-facing materials have emphasized the token and incentive design, this was done primarily to illustrate how decentralization and governance will function at scale. However, the core technology — including the zk-ID framework, Watchtower nodes, and Layer 3 architecture — has been in development for over a year, with internal test environments already in place.
We acknowledge that this could have been communicated more clearly, and we’re working to publish expanded technical documentation and public repositories to make the state of progress more visible.

We recognize the confusion around the “Layer 3” terminology. Here’s the clarification:
Zekret introduces a purpose-built Layer 2 for Cardano, optimized for modular compliance and institutional tooling.
The “Layer 3” we refer to is a modular execution and governance layer, built on top of that L2 — designed to host privacy-preserving compliance apps and decentralized services.
This architecture preserves compatibility with Cardano’s eUTXO model and is engineered to interoperate directly with Cardano’s base layer and smart contract tooling. We’ll be updating our communications to reflect this architecture more explicitly and avoid confusion.

While a core team has spearheaded the initial development, all protocol-level infrastructure, including the zk-ID tooling, node APIs, and governance framework, will be placed under a not-for-profit foundation. This foundation will ensure:
- Open-source licensing for all code.
- Community-aligned governance over infrastructure parameters.
- No license-gated or permissioned barriers to participation.
The long-term vision is not to profit from exclusivity, but to enable decentralized compliance as a public good within Cardano.

That said, your feedback is constructive, and we will consider it as we move forward. We plan to resubmit with more explicit integration materials, live testnet demos, and more visible ecosystem partnerships to demonstrate Zekret’s readiness and value to Cardano.
Thank you again for engaging with the proposal. We look forward to continuing the conversation in future rounds.

We understand the concern around the project’s timeline. However, it’s important to clarify that the 9-month roadmap is not the beginning of our journey — it represents the final stretch of a development cycle already well underway.
Zekret’s core components — including the zk-ID system, Watchtower architecture, and our custom Cardano-compatible Layer 2 — have been under development and internal testing for some time. The proposed 9 months are allocated for:

Final integration of these components.
- Launch and monitoring of a public testnet.
- Onboarding of pilot partners.
- Completion of a mainnet-ready version with full open-source documentation.
We believe this is realistic given our current level of technical readiness.

You’re right — clearly defined KPIs are essential for tracking progress and building trust.
Before the grant’s activation, we will release a detailed KPI matrix including:

- Technical KPIs: Successful integration with Cardano Layer 2, SDK/API release, zk-ID/Watchtower node deployment.
- Community KPIs: Number of external node operators, developer integrations, and institutional sandbox trials.
- Governance KPIs: Open-source milestones, public roadmap transparency, and the transition to community-led oversight via the foundation.
- These metrics will be tracked publicly, with community updates at regular intervals throughout the timeline.

In summary, while we respect the caution, we are confident that Zekret is positioned to meet the proposed milestones — and we are committed to doing so in a way that’s transparent, accountable, and aligned with the long-term goals of the Cardano ecosystem.
Thank you again for your engagement and feedback.

Thank you @surewealthng for highlighting this point — we completely agree that compliance infrastructure should not come at the cost of decentralization or openness, especially within the Cardano ecosystem.

To clarify: Zekret is not a closed-source or license-gated system. In fact, the entire protocol — including the zk-ID system, Watchtower node logic, Layer 2 integration, and developer SDKs — is being released as fully open-source software under permissive licensing (MIT/Apache 2.0).
Furthermore, Zekret is being transitioned into a not-for-profit foundation, which will:

- Govern the protocol transparently.
- Ensure ongoing open-source maintenance.
- Enable any community member, institution, or developer to run nodes, build on top of the infrastructure, or audit the code without restrictions.

Our aim is to empower institutional-grade compliance that preserves privacy, remains permissionless, and aligns with Cardano’s core values of openness, decentralization, and transparency.
We appreciate your alignment with the need for private compliance systems — and we’re committed to delivering them in a way that strengthens, rather than compromises, the open infrastructure of Cardano.

While Project Catalyst is a valuable engine for experimentation and ideation, the Zekret proposal is well beyond the proof-of-concept stage. Much of the underlying architecture — including our zk-ID module, Watchtower node logic, and Layer 3 compliance framework — has already been developed and tested.
The focus of this proposal is to:
- Finalize and deploy a custom Layer 2 built specifically for Cardano.
- Integrate the Layer 3 compliance tooling into that environment.
- Launch to mainnet with full open-source deliverables.

This is not an R&D grant — it is a deployment and ecosystem alignment initiative, which fits the purpose of Core funding more appropriately than Catalyst, whose community voting structure often favors high-visibility over infrastructure-depth.

The Core budget supports proposals that address critical infrastructure gaps, align with Cardano’s strategic roadmap, and offer ecosystem-wide utility. Zekret meets all three:

1. Critical Infrastructure for Regulatory Readiness
- Zekret enables privacy-preserving compliance, aligning with MiCA, FATF, and future institutional adoption needs.
- This addresses one of Cardano’s largest current blockers: regulatory operability at scale.

2. Roadmap-Aligned with Cardano’s Vision
- Our modular Layer 3 will be built atop a new Cardano Layer 2 designed around the eUTXO model, ensuring compatibility and scalability.
- Zekret is strategically aligned with Cardano’s emphasis on interoperability, real-world use cases, and institutional onboarding.


3.Ecosystem-Wide Enablement
- All tooling — including zk-ID SDKs, Watchtower nodes, and APIs — will be open-source and reusable by other projects.
- Governance will be handled by a not-for-profit foundation, ensuring neutrality and long-term accessibility.

In essence, we chose Core funding because Zekret is ready to deliver infrastructure, not just explore it. The platform we’re building is designed to serve Cardano broadly, not just a single use case — and that is precisely the type of initiative Core funding was created to support.
We remain committed to transparency, decentralization, and alignment with the community’s expectations, and we appreciate your consideration and engagement.
